title: The Constraints of Fresco
body:
Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them. The painter applied pigments suspended in water onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp. As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it. The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

The most immediate of these was time. Plaster remained receptive for a matter of hours, so a painter could prepare only as much wall as could be finished in a single session, an area known as a giornata, or day's work. Once the surface had set, further additions would not bond, and a passage judged unsatisfactory could be corrected only by chiseling away the plaster and beginning again. Fresco therefore rewarded certainty and punished hesitation. Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

Pigments presented a second constraint. The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions. Blue was especially troublesome. The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg. Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away. The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

These demands shaped the organization of labor as much as the appearance of the finished work. Because a large wall could not be executed by a single hand within the interval the plaster allowed, fresco encouraged the workshop, in which assistants prepared surfaces, transferred designs, and executed subordinate passages while the master reserved the faces and gestures that carried the meaning of the picture. When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments. That fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward suggests that painters valued something the newer medium could not supply, an image that was not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it.

questions.question: According to paragraph 1, what makes the surface of a buon fresco so durable?

choices.A: The plaster is applied in unusually thick layers before painting begins.
choices.B: A chemical reaction encloses the pigment particles inside the wall itself.
choices.C: The pigments are ground more finely than those used in other media.
choices.D: A protective varnish is brushed over the painting once the plaster dries.

questions.explanation: 第1段落に "lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it" とあり、耐久性の理由は化学反応によって顔料が壁の内部に閉じ込められることだと明示されている。A(厚塗り)、C(顔料の細かさ)、D(ワニス)はいずれも本文に記述がない。

questions.question: The word "these" in paragraph 2 ("The most immediate of these was time") refers to

choices.B: the walls that carried the images
choices.C: the constraints imposed by the chemistry of fresco
choices.D: the particles of color locked within the wall

questions.explanation: 直前の第1段落末尾が "the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made" で終わっており、"these" はこの constraints を受けている。実際、続く第2段落は時間という制約を説明しているため、Cが正しい。Aは制約が支配する対象であって制約そのものではない。

questions.question: The word "denuded" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: 直前で青の絵具層が "centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away" と述べられており、denuded はその結果として色を失った状態を指す。したがって D の stripped bare が最も近い。A の darkened は逆に色が濃くなる方向、B と C は本文の文脈と無関係である。

questions.question: What can be inferred from paragraph 3 about the appearance of certain early Italian chapels when they were first completed?

choices.A: Their skies were more strongly colored than they are today.
choices.B: Their painters deliberately avoided depicting the sky.
choices.C: They contained no passages painted on dried plaster.
choices.D: Their walls were left unfinished for lack of suitable pigments.

questions.explanation: 本文は淡い空が "not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss" だと述べている。つまり画家は青を控えたのではなく、後から塗られた青が失われた結果である。よって完成当初はより濃い青であったと推論できる。Bは "restraint" を否定する本文と矛盾し、Cは青がまさに乾いた漆喰の上に塗られたという記述に反する。

questions.question: Why does the author mention oil painting in paragraph 4?

choices.A: To argue that oil painting quickly replaced fresco throughout Italy
choices.B: To identify, by contrast, the limitations under which fresco painters worked
choices.C: To explain how workshops trained their assistants in a second medium
choices.D: To show that oil painting was invented in response to the failures of fresco

questions.explanation: 油彩は "precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments" として提示されており、本文がそれまでに述べてきた三つの制約(時間・修正不可・顔料の制限)を対比によって際立たせる役割を担っている。Aは "fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward" と矛盾する。Dの起源に関する主張は本文にない。

appearance.etymology: ラテン語 ad-(〜に向かって) + parere(現れる) → appear + -ance(名詞化)
appearance.usage_in_passage: 冒頭の "Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era" で、フレスコが一時代の美術の「見え方」そのものを決めたという主張を導入する語。
appearance.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

decisively.etymology: ラテン語 de-(離して) + caedere(切る) → decide「切り分けて決める」+ -ive + -ly
decisively.usage_in_passage: "shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco" と比較構文を強め、フレスコの影響力が他の技法を上回ることを示す。
decisively.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

buon.etymology: イタリア語 buono「良い」< ラテン語 bonus(良い)
buon.definition: 「良い」を意味するイタリア語。buon fresco で「真正のフレスコ技法」を指す。
buon.usage_in_passage: "buon fresco" という専門用語の一部として登場し、乾いた壁に描く secco 技法と区別される本来のフレスコを指す。
buon.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

fresco.etymology: イタリア語 fresco「新鮮な、生乾きの」(ゲルマン語起源。英語 fresh と同系)
fresco.definition: 生乾きの漆喰に描く壁画技法。
fresco.usage_in_passage: 本文全体の主題語。語源が示すとおり「生乾きのうちに描く」ことが、以降で論じられる時間の制約すべての出発点になっている。
fresco.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

painters.etymology: 古フランス語 peindre < ラテン語 pingere(描く) → paint + -er + -s
painters.usage_in_passage: "Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls" で行為の主体として示され、以後この制約下で働く職人集団として繰り返し言及される。
painters.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

bound.etymology: 古英語 bindan(縛る)の過去分詞形。ゲルマン系の語で、ラテン語由来ではない
bound.definition: 固く結びつけた、定着させた。
bound.usage_in_passage: "bound images permanently into the walls" で、絵が壁の表面に乗るのではなく内部に結合することを示し、第1段落の化学的説明を予告する。
bound.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

permanently.etymology: ラテン語 per-(通して、ずっと) + manere(留まる) → permanent + -ly
permanently.usage_in_passage: "bound images permanently into the walls" で耐久性という長所を提示し、その代償として制約が生じるという本文の骨格を作る。
permanently.context_sentence: Few techniques have shaped the appearance of an era as decisively as buon fresco, the method by which Italian painters bound images permanently into the walls that carried them.

painter.etymology: 古フランス語 peindre < ラテン語 pingere(描く) + -er
painter.usage_in_passage: "The painter applied pigments suspended in water" のように、技法上の判断を下す主体として単数形で繰り返し現れる。
painter.context_sentence: The painter applied pigments suspended in water onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp.

pigments.etymology: ラテン語 pingere(描く) → pigmentum(絵の具) + -s
pigments.definition: 顔料。色を与える粉末の材料。
pigments.usage_in_passage: 第1段落では水に溶いて塗る材料として、第3段落では石灰に耐えられるかどうかで選別される対象として登場し、二つの制約を結ぶ語となっている。
pigments.context_sentence: The painter applied pigments suspended in water onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp.

suspended.etymology: ラテン語 sus-(sub- 下に) + pendere(吊るす) → 「液中に漂わせる」
suspended.definition: (液体中に)分散させた、懸濁させた。
suspended.usage_in_passage: "pigments suspended in water" で、顔料が水に溶けるのではなく粒子として漂っている状態を正確に述べ、後の「粒子が壁に閉じ込められる」という説明につながる。
suspended.context_sentence: The painter applied pigments suspended in water onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp.

plaster.etymology: ギリシャ語 emplastron「塗りつけるもの」< en-(上に) + plassein(形づくる)
plaster.definition: 漆喰。壁に塗る石灰と砂の混合物。
plaster.usage_in_passage: 本文の中心的な物質。"onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp" とあるように、その乾燥速度が画家の作業時間を規定する。
plaster.context_sentence: The painter applied pigments suspended in water onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp.

damp.etymology: 中低ドイツ語 damp「蒸気」に由来するゲルマン系の語
damp.usage_in_passage: "while it remained damp" が buon fresco の必須条件を一語で示し、この状態が失われた時点で作業が終わることを含意する。
damp.context_sentence: The painter applied pigments suspended in water onto a layer of plaster while it remained damp.

dried.etymology: 古英語 dryge(乾いた) → dry + -ed。ゲルマン系
dried.usage_in_passage: "As the plaster dried" が第1段落の化学反応を導く時間節となり、乾燥が単なる水分の消失ではなく化学変化の過程であることを示す。
dried.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

lime.etymology: 古英語 lim「粘着物」。ゲルマン系の語で、果物の lime とは別語源
lime.definition: 石灰。漆喰の主成分となる強アルカリ性の物質。
lime.usage_in_passage: "lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide" で耐久性の源として、第3段落では "The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors" で顔料を壊す元凶として現れ、同じ物質が長所と短所の両方を生むという本文の逆説を担う。
lime.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

mortar.etymology: ラテン語 mortarium「臼、そこで作られる漆喰」
mortar.definition: モルタル。石灰と砂を練った建材。
mortar.usage_in_passage: "lime in the mortar" として、反応を起こす石灰がどこに含まれているかを特定する。
mortar.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

reacted.etymology: ラテン語 re-(再び、応じて) + agere(行う) → react + -ed
reacted.usage_in_passage: "lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide" が、フレスコの耐久性が物理的な付着ではなく化学変化によることを明示する中核の動詞。
reacted.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

carbon.usage_in_passage: "carbon dioxide drawn from the air" で、壁を硬化させる反応相手が空気中の気体であることを示す。
carbon.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

dioxide.etymology: ギリシャ語 di-(二つの) + oxide(酸化物) → 酸素原子を二つ含む化合物
dioxide.definition: 二酸化物。ここでは二酸化炭素。
dioxide.usage_in_passage: "carbon dioxide drawn from the air" として、フレスコの硬化が外気を取り込む過程であることを説明する。
dioxide.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

drawn.etymology: 古英語 dragan(引く)の過去分詞。ゲルマン系
drawn.definition: 引き出された、取り込まれた。
drawn.usage_in_passage: "carbon dioxide drawn from the air" で、反応に必要な気体が外部から供給されることを示し、壁が周囲の環境と反応する開いた系であることを示唆する。
drawn.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

crystalline.etymology: ギリシャ語 krystallos「氷、水晶」+ -ine(〜からなる)
crystalline.usage_in_passage: "a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate" で、生成物が非晶質の膜ではなく結晶構造をもつことを示し、耐久性の根拠を具体化する。
crystalline.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

calcium.etymology: ラテン語 calx「石灰、小石」+ 元素名を作る -ium
calcium.usage_in_passage: "calcium carbonate" として、石灰と二酸化炭素の反応生成物を化学名で特定する。
calcium.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

carbonate.usage_in_passage: "a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate" が、顔料を封じ込める物質の正体を示す。
carbonate.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

locking.etymology: 古英語 loc「錠、留め具」→ lock + -ing。ゲルマン系
locking.definition: 閉じ込めること、固定すること。
locking.usage_in_passage: "locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it" が第1段落の要点。within と upon の対比によって、フレスコが表面塗装ではないことを決定づける。
locking.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

particles.etymology: ラテン語 pars(部分)の縮小形 particula + -s
particles.usage_in_passage: "the particles of color" が、封じ込められる対象が溶けた色素ではなく固体の粒であることを示し、suspended in water の記述と呼応する。
particles.context_sentence: As the plaster dried, lime in the mortar reacted with carbon dioxide drawn from the air and formed a crystalline skin of calcium carbonate, locking the particles of color within the wall rather than upon it.

extraordinarily.etymology: ラテン語 extra-(外の) + ordinarius(通常の) → extraordinary + -ly
extraordinarily.usage_in_passage: "The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable" で長所を最大限に述べ、直後の but による転換を際立たせる。
extraordinarily.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

durable.etymology: ラテン語 durare(持続する) < durus(硬い) + -able
durable.usage_in_passage: フレスコの唯一最大の利点を示す語で、この一語のために画家が受け入れた代償が本文の残り全体を占める。
durable.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

chemistry.etymology: アラビア語 al-kīmiyā → alchemy → chemist + -ry
chemistry.usage_in_passage: "the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints" が本文の主題文。同一の化学的性質が恩恵と制約の両方の源であるという逆説を一文で提示する。
chemistry.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

conferred.etymology: ラテン語 con-(共に) + ferre(運ぶ) → 「与える、授ける」
conferred.usage_in_passage: "the chemistry that conferred this permanence" で、耐久性が偶然ではなく化学から必然的に与えられたものであることを示す。
conferred.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

permanence.etymology: ラテン語 per-(ずっと) + manere(留まる) + -ence(名詞化)
permanence.usage_in_passage: 第1段落冒頭の permanently を名詞で受け直し、主題文において「何が制約と引き換えに得られたのか」を明示する。
permanence.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

imposed.etymology: ラテン語 im-(in- 上に) + ponere(置く) → 「課す」
imposed.usage_in_passage: "also imposed constraints" が主題文の後半で、恩恵と同じ原因から負担が生じるという構造を作る。
imposed.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

constraints.etymology: ラテン語 con-(共に) + stringere(締めつける) → 「締めて動きを制限するもの」+ -s
constraints.usage_in_passage: 本文を貫くキーワード。第2段落の時間、第3段落の顔料、第4段落の労働編成という三つの制約がすべてこの語に集約される。
constraints.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

governed.etymology: ラテン語 gubernare(舵を取る) < ギリシャ語 kybernan → govern + -ed
governed.usage_in_passage: "constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made" で、制約が技法上の細部ではなく判断の全体に及ぶことを示す。
governed.context_sentence: The resulting surface was extraordinarily durable, but the chemistry that conferred this permanence also imposed constraints that governed nearly every decision the painter made.

immediate.etymology: ラテン語 im-(否定) + mediatus(仲介された) → 「間に何もない」
immediate.usage_in_passage: "The most immediate of these was time" で三つの制約に順序を与え、時間を最優先の論点として提示する。
immediate.context_sentence: The most immediate of these was time.

receptive.etymology: ラテン語 re-(再び) + capere(取る) → recept- + -ive
receptive.definition: 受け入れられる状態の。
receptive.usage_in_passage: "Plaster remained receptive for a matter of hours" で、漆喰が絵の具を受け付ける時間が限られていることを述べ、giornata の説明を導く。
receptive.context_sentence: Plaster remained receptive for a matter of hours, so a painter could prepare only as much wall as could be finished in a single session, an area known as a giornata, or day's work.

prepare.etymology: ラテン語 prae-(前もって) + parare(整える)
prepare.usage_in_passage: "a painter could prepare only as much wall as could be finished in a single session" で、塗る面積そのものが時間から逆算されることを示す。
prepare.context_sentence: Plaster remained receptive for a matter of hours, so a painter could prepare only as much wall as could be finished in a single session, an area known as a giornata, or day's work.

giornata.etymology: イタリア語 giorno「日」< ラテン語 diurnus(一日の) + -ata → 「一日分の仕事」
giornata.definition: ジョルナータ。一日で仕上げられる漆喰の区画。
giornata.usage_in_passage: "an area known as a giornata, or day's work" が、時間の制約が物理的な区画として壁に刻まれることを示す専門用語。
giornata.context_sentence: Plaster remained receptive for a matter of hours, so a painter could prepare only as much wall as could be finished in a single session, an area known as a giornata, or day's work.

day's.etymology: 古英語 dæg(日) + 所有を表す -'s。ゲルマン系
day's.usage_in_passage: "a giornata, or day's work" と言い換えることで、イタリア語の専門用語を平易に説明している。
day's.context_sentence: Plaster remained receptive for a matter of hours, so a painter could prepare only as much wall as could be finished in a single session, an area known as a giornata, or day's work.

bond.etymology: 中英語 band「縛るもの」。bind と同系のゲルマン語
bond.usage_in_passage: "further additions would not bond" で、時間切れ後の加筆が物理的に不可能であることを示し、修正できないという次の論点へつなぐ。
bond.context_sentence: Once the surface had set, further additions would not bond, and a passage judged unsatisfactory could be corrected only by chiseling away the plaster and beginning again.

passage.etymology: ラテン語 passus(歩み) → pass + -age
passage.usage_in_passage: "a passage judged unsatisfactory" では絵の一区画を指す。第3段落の "Such passages" も同じ用法で、青を後から塗った箇所を指す。
passage.context_sentence: Once the surface had set, further additions would not bond, and a passage judged unsatisfactory could be corrected only by chiseling away the plaster and beginning again.

unsatisfactory.etymology: un-(否定) + ラテン語 satis(十分) + facere(作る) → satisfactory の否定
unsatisfactory.usage_in_passage: "a passage judged unsatisfactory could be corrected only by chiseling away the plaster" で、失敗の代償が壁の破壊であることを示す。
unsatisfactory.context_sentence: Once the surface had set, further additions would not bond, and a passage judged unsatisfactory could be corrected only by chiseling away the plaster and beginning again.

chiseling.etymology: 古フランス語 cisel「のみ」< ラテン語 caedere(切る) + -ing
chiseling.usage_in_passage: 修正の唯一の方法として提示され、"rewarded certainty and punished hesitation" という次の一文の根拠になっている。
chiseling.context_sentence: Once the surface had set, further additions would not bond, and a passage judged unsatisfactory could be corrected only by chiseling away the plaster and beginning again.

rewarded.etymology: re-(再び) + 古北フランス語 warder(見張る) → 「報いる」
rewarded.usage_in_passage: "Fresco therefore rewarded certainty and punished hesitation" の対句の前半。技法が画家の資質を選別することを示す。
rewarded.context_sentence: Fresco therefore rewarded certainty and punished hesitation.

certainty.etymology: ラテン語 cernere(識別する) → certus(確かな) + -ty
certainty.usage_in_passage: 対句の中で hesitation と対置され、フレスコが要求する心理的態度を名指す。
certainty.context_sentence: Fresco therefore rewarded certainty and punished hesitation.

punished.usage_in_passage: "punished hesitation" が対句の後半で、迷いが取り返しのつかない損失に直結することを示す。
punished.context_sentence: Fresco therefore rewarded certainty and punished hesitation.

hesitation.etymology: ラテン語 haerere(くっつく、ためらう) → haesitare + -ion
hesitation.usage_in_passage: certainty と対をなし、通常の絵画では許される試行錯誤がフレスコでは成立しないことを示す。
hesitation.context_sentence: Fresco therefore rewarded certainty and punished hesitation.

composition.etymology: ラテン語 com-(共に) + ponere(置く) + -ition → 「組み立てること」
composition.definition: 構図。画面内の要素の配置。
composition.usage_in_passage: "Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings" で、制作の順序が逆転すること、すなわち考える作業が壁の前から下絵へ移ることを示す。
composition.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

resolved.etymology: ラテン語 re-(強意) + solvere(解く) → 「解決する」
resolved.definition: 決着をつけた、確定した。
resolved.usage_in_passage: "resolved in advance" が、壁の上での判断が許されないという第2段落の帰結を要約する。
resolved.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

drawings.etymology: 古英語 dragan(引く) → draw + -ing + -s。ゲルマン系
drawings.usage_in_passage: 壁の前で試せない分の思考を引き受ける媒体として提示され、ルネサンス美術で素描が重視された理由を示唆する。
drawings.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

transferred.etymology: ラテン語 trans-(越えて) + ferre(運ぶ)
transferred.usage_in_passage: "the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically" で、下絵から壁への移行が創造ではなく機械的作業であることを示す。
transferred.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

mechanically.etymology: ギリシャ語 mēkhanē(装置) → mechanical + -ly
mechanically.definition: 機械的に、手順に従って。
mechanically.usage_in_passage: 転写が判断を伴わない工程であることを示し、次に挙げる二つの具体的手法を導く。
mechanically.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

incising.etymology: ラテン語 in-(中に) + caedere(切る) → 「刻み込む」
incising.usage_in_passage: "either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface" が転写手法の一つ目で、生乾きの漆喰の柔らかさを利用する方法である。
incising.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

outlines.etymology: out(外) + line(< ラテン語 linea 糸)。ゲルマン語とラテン語の複合
outlines.usage_in_passage: 転写されるのが陰影ではなく輪郭であることを示し、色の判断が壁の上に残されることを含意する。
outlines.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

dusting.etymology: 古英語 dūst(塵) → dust + -ing。ゲルマン系
dusting.usage_in_passage: "by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet" が転写手法の二つ目(ポウンス法)で、漆喰を傷つけずに下絵を写す方法である。
dusting.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

charcoal.etymology: char(焦がす) + coal(炭)。ゲルマン系の複合語
charcoal.usage_in_passage: 穴を通して落とす粉として用いられ、消しやすさゆえに転写に適していることが含意される。
charcoal.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

perforated.etymology: ラテン語 per-(通して) + forare(穴を開ける) + -ate
perforated.usage_in_passage: "a perforated sheet" が、下絵の輪郭に沿って針で穴を空けた紙(カルトン)を指し、転写の仕組みを説明する。
perforated.context_sentence: Composition had to be resolved in advance through drawings, and the finished design was transferred to the wall mechanically, either by incising its outlines into the fresh surface or by dusting charcoal through a perforated sheet.

constraint.etymology: ラテン語 con-(共に) + stringere(締めつける)
constraint.usage_in_passage: "Pigments presented a second constraint" が第3段落の主題文となり、時間に続く二つ目の制約を明示的に数える。

alkalinity.etymology: アラビア語 al-qalī「(植物を焼いた)灰」→ alkali + -ine + -ity
alkalinity.usage_in_passage: "The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors" で、第1段落では長所の源だった石灰が、ここでは顔料を破壊する原因として再登場する。
alkalinity.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

destroyed.etymology: ラテン語 de-(下に) + struere(積み上げる) → 「積んだものを崩す」
destroyed.usage_in_passage: 顔料が単に変色するのではなく化学的に壊れることを示し、代替手段を取らざるを得ない理由を与える。
destroyed.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

freely.etymology: 古英語 frēo(自由な) → free + -ly。ゲルマン系
freely.usage_in_passage: "colors that painters used freely in other media" が他技法との対比を作り、制約がフレスコ固有であることを際立たせる。
freely.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

palette.etymology: ラテン語 pala(へら)の縮小形 palette
palette.definition: パレット。転じて、使用できる色の範囲。
palette.usage_in_passage: "the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow" で、制約の帰結が画家の色彩選択の幅そのものであることを示す。
palette.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

consequently.etymology: ラテン語 con-(共に) + sequi(従う) → consequent + -ly
consequently.usage_in_passage: アルカリによる破壊という原因と、色数が限られるという結果を明示的に接続する論理標識。
consequently.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

narrow.etymology: 古英語 nearu(狭い)。ゲルマン系
narrow.usage_in_passage: palette を修飾し、豊かさではなく乏しさがフレスコの色彩を特徴づけることを述べる。
narrow.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

dominated.etymology: ラテン語 dominus(主人) → dominari + -ed
dominated.definition: 大半を占めた、支配的だった。
dominated.usage_in_passage: "dominated by earths and other minerals" が、限られた色数の内訳を具体的に示す。
dominated.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

minerals.etymology: 中世ラテン語 minerale(鉱石) < mine(採掘する) + -s
minerals.usage_in_passage: 土性顔料とともに、アルカリに耐える数少ない材料として挙げられる。
minerals.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

tolerated.usage_in_passage: "minerals that tolerated caustic conditions" が、顔料の選別基準が美的なものではなく化学的耐性であることを示す。
tolerated.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

caustic.etymology: ギリシャ語 kaustikos(焼く) < kaiein(燃やす)
caustic.definition: 腐食性の、焼けつくような。
caustic.usage_in_passage: 石灰の環境の過酷さを一語で示し、なぜ多くの顔料が使えないのかを感覚的にも伝える。
caustic.context_sentence: The alkalinity of wet lime destroyed many colors that painters used freely in other media, and the palette available for true fresco was consequently narrow, dominated by earths and other minerals that tolerated caustic conditions.

troublesome.etymology: trouble(< ラテン語 turbidus かき乱された) + -some(〜をもたらす)
troublesome.usage_in_passage: "Blue was especially troublesome" が段落内の焦点を青一色に絞り込み、以降の具体例を導く転換点となる。

yielded.etymology: 古英語 gieldan(支払う、産出する)。ゲルマン系
yielded.usage_in_passage: "The pigments that yielded convincing blues" で、望ましい色を出せる顔料と石灰に耐える顔料が一致しないという矛盾を示す。
yielded.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

convincing.etymology: ラテン語 con-(強意) + vincere(打ち負かす) → convince + -ing
convincing.definition: 説得力のある、本物らしい。
convincing.usage_in_passage: 青の色調が代替品では satisfactory にならなかったことを示し、画家が危険を承知で secco 技法を選んだ理由を説明する。
convincing.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

survive.etymology: ラテン語 super-(超えて) + vivere(生きる)
survive.definition: 生き延びる、持ちこたえる。
survive.usage_in_passage: "did not survive contact with lime" で、青の顔料が石灰と共存できないという事実を述べ、以下の回避策につなぐ。
survive.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

obliged.etymology: ラテン語 ob-(に向かって) + ligare(縛る) → 「義務を負わせる」
obliged.usage_in_passage: "painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured" が、secco 技法の採用が選好ではなく強制であったことを示す。
obliged.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

cured.etymology: ラテン語 cura(世話) → curare。ここでは材料が化学的に硬化する意
cured.definition: 硬化した、養生を終えた。
cured.usage_in_passage: "after the plaster had cured" で、青が塗られる時点ではもう化学的結合が起きないことを示し、後の剥落の伏線となる。
cured.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

binder.etymology: 古英語 bindan(縛る) → bind + -er。ゲルマン系
binder.definition: 展色剤。顔料を固着させる媒剤。
binder.usage_in_passage: "using a binder of glue or egg" が、石灰に代わる接着手段を示すと同時に、その接着が有機物頼みで脆いことを含意する。
binder.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

glue.definition: 膠(にかわ)。動物性の接着剤。
glue.usage_in_passage: 卵とともに secco 技法の展色剤として挙げられ、湿気に弱い有機素材であることが後の損失につながる。
glue.context_sentence: The pigments that yielded convincing blues did not survive contact with lime, and painters were obliged to apply them after the plaster had cured, using a binder of glue or egg.

passages.etymology: ラテン語 passus(歩み) → pass + -age + -s
passages.usage_in_passage: "Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated" で、青の部分が壁と一体化していないという決定的な差を述べる。
passages.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

attached.etymology: 古フランス語 estachier(杭で留める)。ゲルマン語 stake と同系
attached.usage_in_passage: chemically incorporated と対置され、mechanically という副詞とともに、青が壁の「上」にとどまることを示す。第4段落末尾の "not merely attached to architecture" と呼応する。
attached.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

chemically.usage_in_passage: attached との対比で用いられ、第1段落の "locking...within the wall rather than upon it" を第3段落で再確認する。
chemically.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

incorporated.etymology: ラテン語 in-(中に) + corpus(体) + -ate → 「体内に取り込む」
incorporated.definition: 一体化した、組み込まれた。
incorporated.usage_in_passage: 青の部分に欠けているものを名指し、なぜそれだけが失われたのかという因果を完成させる。
incorporated.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

centuries.usage_in_passage: "centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away" で、損失が事故ではなく時間の必然であることを示す。
centuries.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

humidity.usage_in_passage: 壁画を長期的に破壊する作用因として提示され、第1段落で壁を硬化させた水分と対をなす。
humidity.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

stripped.etymology: 中英語 stripen(剥ぎ取る)。ゲルマン系
stripped.usage_in_passage: "have stripped many of them away" が損失を能動的な剥奪として描き、直後の denuded の語義を文脈から導く手がかりになっている。
stripped.context_sentence: Such passages were mechanically attached rather than chemically incorporated, and centuries of humidity have stripped many of them away.

pale.etymology: ラテン語 pallidus(青白い) < pallere(青ざめる)
pale.usage_in_passage: "The pale, denuded skies" が、鑑賞者が目にする現状を描写し、それが原状ではないという段落の結論を導く。
pale.context_sentence: The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

denuded.etymology: ラテン語 de-(完全に) + nudare(裸にする) < nudus(裸の)
denuded.definition: 剥き出しにされた、覆いを失った。
denuded.usage_in_passage: 語彙問題の対象語。直前の "stripped many of them away" が語義の手がかりとなり、空が本来もっていた青の層を失った状態を指す。
denuded.context_sentence: The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

admire.etymology: ラテン語 ad-(に対して) + mirari(驚く、見とれる)
admire.usage_in_passage: "skies that visitors now admire" に皮肉が込められている。鑑賞者が画家の美意識と信じているものが、実は損傷の結果だという段落の主張を成立させる語。
admire.context_sentence: The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

chapels.etymology: 後期ラテン語 cappella「小さな外套」。聖マルティヌスの外套を納めた聖堂に由来 + -s
chapels.usage_in_passage: "certain early Italian chapels" が、議論を抽象論から実在する作品へ引き寄せ、推論問題の舞台を与える。
chapels.context_sentence: The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

restraint.etymology: ラテン語 re-(後ろへ) + stringere(締めつける) → 「引き止めること」
restraint.usage_in_passage: "not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss" で、二つの解釈を対置する。この否定こそが推論問題の根拠となる。
restraint.context_sentence: The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

painter's.usage_in_passage: "on the painter's part" が、抑制という解釈の主体を画家に帰し、それを否定することで責任を時間と湿気に移す。
painter's.context_sentence: The pale, denuded skies that visitors now admire in certain early Italian chapels are not evidence of restraint on the painter's part but of loss.

executed.etymology: ラテン語 ex-(外に) + sequi(従う) → exsequi(遂行する) + -ed
executed.usage_in_passage: "could not be executed by a single hand within the interval" が第4段落の主題文で、時間の制約が労働の編成にまで及ぶことを示す。
executed.context_sentence: Because a large wall could not be executed by a single hand within the interval the plaster allowed, fresco encouraged the workshop, in which assistants prepared surfaces, transferred designs, and executed subordinate passages while the master reserved the faces and gestures that carried the meaning of the picture.

interval.etymology: ラテン語 inter-(間) + vallum(城壁) → 「柵と柵の間」
interval.usage_in_passage: 第2段落の a matter of hours を言い換え、時間の制約が第4段落の議論の前提として再導入されることを示す。
interval.context_sentence: Because a large wall could not be executed by a single hand within the interval the plaster allowed, fresco encouraged the workshop, in which assistants prepared surfaces, transferred designs, and executed subordinate passages while the master reserved the faces and gestures that carried the meaning of the picture.

encouraged.etymology: en-(与える) + courage(< ラテン語 cor 心) + -ed
encouraged.usage_in_passage: "fresco encouraged the workshop" が、技法が組織形態を生むという本文で最も大きな主張を担う動詞。強制ではなく誘導であることを含意する。
encouraged.context_sentence: Because a large wall could not be executed by a single hand within the interval the plaster allowed, fresco encouraged the workshop, in which assistants prepared surfaces, transferred designs, and executed subordinate passages while the master reserved the faces and gestures that carried the meaning of the picture.

subordinate.etymology: ラテン語 sub-(下に) + ordinare(順序づける)
subordinate.definition: 従属的な、重要度の低い。
subordinate.usage_in_passage: "executed subordinate passages" が工房内の分業を示し、直後の "the master reserved the faces and gestures" との対比で価値の序列を明らかにする。
subordinate.context_sentence: Because a large wall could not be executed by a single hand within the interval the plaster allowed, fresco encouraged the workshop, in which assistants prepared surfaces, transferred designs, and executed subordinate passages while the master reserved the faces and gestures that carried the meaning of the picture.

gestures.etymology: ラテン語 gerere(行う、振る舞う) → gestura + -s
gestures.usage_in_passage: faces と並んで親方が自ら描く要素として挙げられ、絵の意味を担う部分がどこかを示す。
gestures.context_sentence: Because a large wall could not be executed by a single hand within the interval the plaster allowed, fresco encouraged the workshop, in which assistants prepared surfaces, transferred designs, and executed subordinate passages while the master reserved the faces and gestures that carried the meaning of the picture.

painting.usage_in_passage: "When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice" で、フレスコに代わる選択肢として油彩を導入する。
painting.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

canvas.etymology: ラテン語 cannabis(大麻) → 麻布
canvas.usage_in_passage: panel とともに、壁から切り離された支持体を示し、絵が建築から独立していく流れを含意する。
canvas.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

spread.etymology: 古英語 sprǣdan(広げる)。ゲルマン系
spread.usage_in_passage: 油彩がイタリアへ伝播したことを述べ、フレスコが唯一の選択肢でなくなった時点を示す。
spread.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

sixteenth.usage_in_passage: "during the sixteenth century" が、それまで技法の論理で進んだ議論に具体的な時代を与える。
sixteenth.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

precisely.etymology: ラテン語 prae-(前もって) + caedere(切る) → 「切り詰められた」→ 正確な
precisely.usage_in_passage: "it offered precisely what fresco withheld" で、油彩の利点がフレスコの欠点の裏返しであることを強調し、続くコロン以下の三点を本文全体の要約として機能させる。
precisely.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

withheld.etymology: with-(後ろへ) + hold(古英語 healdan)の過去分詞。ゲルマン系
withheld.definition: 与えなかった、差し控えた。
withheld.usage_in_passage: フレスコを能動的な主語として描くことで、制約が単なる欠陥ではなく技法の性格であるという含みを与える。
withheld.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

slowly.etymology: 古英語 slāw(鈍い) → slow + -ly。ゲルマン系
slowly.usage_in_passage: "a medium that dried slowly" が油彩の第一の利点で、第2段落の時間の制約に正確に対応する。
slowly.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

admitted.etymology: ラテン語 ad-(に) + mittere(送る) → 「入れる」
admitted.usage_in_passage: "admitted the full range of pigments" が油彩の第三の利点で、第3段落の顔料の制約に対応する。三つの利点が三つの制約に順に対応する構造を完成させる。
admitted.context_sentence: When oil painting on panel and canvas spread into Italian practice during the sixteenth century, it offered precisely what fresco withheld: a medium that dried slowly, accepted revision, and admitted the full range of pigments.

nevertheless.etymology: never + the + less の複合。ゲルマン系
nevertheless.usage_in_passage: "That fresco nevertheless persisted" が、油彩の優位を認めた上で反転を導入し、本文最後の主張への転換点となる。
nevertheless.context_sentence: That fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward suggests that painters valued something the newer medium could not supply, an image that was not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it.

persisted.etymology: ラテン語 per-(通して) + sistere(立つ) → 「立ち続ける」
persisted.definition: 存続した、使われ続けた。
persisted.usage_in_passage: より便利な媒体が現れてもフレスコが残ったという事実を提示し、それを説明する必要が最終文の主張を要請する。
persisted.context_sentence: That fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward suggests that painters valued something the newer medium could not supply, an image that was not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it.

afterward.etymology: after + 方向を表す -ward。ゲルマン系
afterward.usage_in_passage: "for generations afterward" が存続の長さを示し、フレスコの残存が一時的な惰性ではないことを示す。
afterward.context_sentence: That fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward suggests that painters valued something the newer medium could not supply, an image that was not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it.

newer.etymology: 古英語 nīwe(新しい) → new + 比較級 -er。ゲルマン系
newer.usage_in_passage: "the newer medium" が油彩を指し、新しさが必ずしも優位を意味しないという最終文の逆説を準備する。
newer.context_sentence: That fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward suggests that painters valued something the newer medium could not supply, an image that was not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it.

merely.etymology: ラテン語 merus(混じりけのない) → mere + -ly
merely.usage_in_passage: "not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it" で、第1段落の within/upon の対比を建築との関係に転用し、本文を主題へ回帰させて締めくくる。
merely.context_sentence: That fresco nevertheless persisted for generations afterward suggests that painters valued something the newer medium could not supply, an image that was not merely attached to architecture but had become part of it.
